boundary_rationale: A second-person-feminine-singular imperative pair opens the unit, “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh's glory has risen on you!” (web:Isa.60.1), matching ק֥וּמִי א֖וֹרִי (oshb:Isa.60.1, byte tier). The same addressee is sustained through further imperative and declarative movements — nations and kings drawn to her light, sons and daughters carried home, foreign wealth and foreign service given to her, her gates kept open — without an explicit change of addressee or scene across the chapter. A recognition-formula clause partway through, “Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.” (web:Isa.60.16), matching וְיָדַ֗עַתְּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.60.16, byte tier), is not repeated at the unit's own close: “I, Yahweh, will do this quickly in its time.” (web:Isa.60.22), matching אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּעִתָּ֥הּ אֲחִישֶֽׁנָּה (oshb:Isa.60.22, byte tier), which carries no knowing-verb at all, so the two clauses share only the two-token self-declaration אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ / אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה — a pairing that differs at byte and at accent-stripped tier and meets only at skeleton tier, where it stands in 22 verses book-wide. Even at that lighter tier, the repeated self-declaration frames an internal turn rather than marking a second addressee. Isa.61.1 opens a new first-person speaker frame, “The Lord Yahweh's Spirit is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble.” (web:Isa.61.1), sharing no addressee with this chapter's second-person Zion address, and closes this unit. This row's span is the entirety of chapter 60 (22 verses in the book's own inventory), so under the campaign's whole-chapter rule its confidence is held at the medium_low ceiling rather than assigned a lower band, and that ceiling reflects the span's shape, not any new defect found in it.

Isa.60.21 stages both the ketiv and qere forms of the planting noun side by side, נֵ֧צֶר מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדַ֖י לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier) — the unpointed ketiv מטעו carries a third-person-masculine-singular suffix ('his planting'), the pointed qere מַטָּעַ֛י a first-person-singular suffix ('my planting'); the two forms differ by suffix person, not number, and this is a single-witness note read either way. The same planting-root vocabulary paired with the 'to be glorified' verb recurs in the following unit's own close (web:Isa.61.3), a catchword this unit's own boundary does not erase. The qadosh-Israel title, a signature title spanning both halves of the book (25 verses swept per attested spelling: 24 at the standard plene spelling, plus the separately-attested defective spelling קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte tier)), recurs at web:Isa.60.9 and web:Isa.60.14 inside this span as in-unit texture, not a boundary driver.

boundary_rationale: A first-person speaker announces a commission, “The Lord Yahweh's Spirit is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble.” (web:Isa.61.1), matching ר֛וּחַ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה עָלָ֑י (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier). A chain of purpose infinitives governed by that same sending — to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty and release, to comfort mourners, to give a garland for ashes — runs to the verse's own caesura at כֵּהָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) and continues, not as a further infinitive but as a waw-plus-perfect finite clause naming the mourners themselves as its subject, וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier): “that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.” (web:Isa.61.3), matching מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier). Isa.61.4 opens a further waw-plus-perfect clause with a changed subject, “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4) — the third-person-plural community now rebuilding, distinct from the mourners just named and called a planting at the unit's own close — marking this unit's close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the first-person mission statement as continuing through Isa.61.4's building report was rejected because the infinitive-purpose chain governed by Yahweh's sending closes at Isa.61.3's own glorification clause, and Isa.61.4 opens a new finite-verb clause with a third-person-plural subject. Labeling the unit servant_song was considered and set aside because this unit's own bytes lack the eved-root vocabulary that anchors the book's servant census, leaving the anointed speaker's identity an open question the unit does not resolve.

boundary_rationale: A new first-person voice opens with rejoicing, “I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh! boundary_rationale: A first-person resolve opens the unit; Zion is named in the third person, “until her righteousness shines out like the dawn, and her salvation like a burning lamp.” (web:Isa.62.1), matching צִדְקָ֔הּ וִישׁוּעָתָ֖הּ (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier). The direct second-person address to Zion begins at the following verse, “The nations will see your righteousness” (web:Isa.62.2), and runs through the renaming and marriage imagery to this unit's own close, “As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.” (web:Isa.62.5). Isa.62.6 introduces a new participant group, the posted watchmen, “I have set watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem.” (web:Isa.62.6), matching שֹֽׁמְרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier), and the speaker's own first-person act shifts from the vow of Isa.62.1 to an act of appointment already completed; the second-person-feminine-singular addressee and the first-person voice both continue unbroken past this seam, so the seam is marked by the new watchmen and the shift from vow to appointment, not by any change of addressee, speaker, or person, closing this unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through Isa.62.6's watchmen scene was rejected because that verse introduces a new participant group, the posted watchmen, and turns the speaker's own first-person act from the vow opening this unit to an act of appointment already completed; the second-person-feminine-singular addressee and the first-person voice both continue unbroken across that seam, so the boundary rests on the new participant group and the vow-to-appointment shift, not on any vocative or change of speaker.

The speaker charges those watchmen, in second-person-plural imperatives addressed to them, to give Yahweh no rest, אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) and וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.7, byte tier); that charge is answered by an oath formula, “Yahweh has sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength,” (web:Isa.62.8), matching נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.62.8, byte tier), that introduces Yahweh's own quoted promise through the unit's close, “Those who have gathered it will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.” (web:Isa.62.9). boundary_rationale: A fresh plural-imperative summons opens the unit, “Go through, go through the gates! Prepare the way of the people!” (web:Isa.62.10), matching עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier). The unit closes on a renaming formula, “They will call them “The Holy People, Yahweh's Redeemed”.” (web:Isa.62.12), matching עַם הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ גְּאוּלֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.62.12, byte tier). boundary_rationale: This unit is bounded by a dramatic question-and-answer frame: the prophetic voice opens with a verse-initial interrogative, מִי זֶ֣ה בָּ֣א מֵאֱד֗וֹם (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier), “Who is this who comes from Edom” (web:Isa.63.1); the clause that follows opens instead on a bare demonstrative, זֶ֚ה הָד֣וּר בִּלְבוּשׁ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier), rendered as a second question, “Who is this who is glorious in his clothing,” only in the English witness. The challenged figure answers in the first person, closing that reply with “אֲנִ֛י מְדַבֵּ֥ר בִּצְדָקָ֖ה רַ֥ב לְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ” (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier) ('I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save'). A further verse-initial interrogative opens the next verse, מַדּ֥וּעַ (oshb:Isa.63.2, byte tier), “Why is your clothing red” (web:Isa.63.2), continuing the exchange. The same first-person divine-warrior voice continues in unbroken speech through the vengeance-and-treading report, closing the unit at “I poured their lifeblood out on the earth.” (web:Isa.63.6). The unit ends there because 63:7 pivots to a different speaker and a different speech-act: a first-person-plural recital of Yahweh's mercies replaces the divine warrior's own first-person report, with no further interrogative sustaining the dialogue frame.

boundary_rationale: The recollection opens with a first-person-singular self-announcing speech-act verb, אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), “I will tell of the loving kindnesses of Yahweh and the praises of Yahweh” (web:Isa.63.7) — the same grammatical person as the preceding unit's own divine-warrior voice, so the seam is marked by the change in speech-act, from the warrior's own action-report to this unit's recital of Yahweh's dealings, not by any change of person. It moves through a historical recital of the Exodus generation — Israel's election, its rebellion, and Moses' generation being led through the depths — naming a holy-spirit phrase twice, אֶת ר֣וּחַ קָדְשׁ֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.63.10, byte tier) and אֶת ר֥וּחַ קָדְשֽׁוֹ (oshb:Isa.63.11, byte tier) ('his Holy Spirit' both times, each with its own governing 'et'), a lexical thread that meets only at skeleton tier — the two occurrences differ at byte tier and at accent-stripped tier, the later one carrying a meteg that accent-stripping retains — binding the rebellion report to the Mosaic memory across 63:10-11 at that lighter tier. The unit closes at “So you led your people to make yourself a glorious name.” (web:Isa.63.14), immediately before the imperative “Look down from heaven” (web:Isa.63.15) pivots the speech from third-person recollection about Yahweh's past acts to a direct second-person petition addressed to Yahweh himself.
